taxonomy.counts_meaning: taxon memberships; one sequence may occur in more than one taxon

source_quality.meaning: reported measurements, separated by method; not category-derived reliability grades

dependence.meaning: groups collapse demonstrated sequence identity; distinct groups are not claimed independent experiments

search_limits.meaning: all supplied hit rows retained; hitting a limit can censor evidence, fewer hits do not establish database completeness

function_weights.conditioning: explicit function assignments among the supplied scored reference sequence groups

search_limits.meaning: all supplied hit rows retained; hitting a limit can censor evidence, fewer hits do not establish database completeness

assumptions: Native bit score differences define a chosen reference-similarity kernel, not a measured functional likelihood.
A native hit or demonstrated duplicate sequence group contributes once using its strongest HSP.
Distinct explicit function labels within a sequence group divide its mass equally; this is not a claim that multifunctional proteins have only one function.
Probabilities are conditional on the supplied candidate functions and returned matches; unreported or unannotated functions remain outside that distribution.
Representation correction uses independently supplied matching database sequence counts; it is not inferred from returned-hit counts.
Unresolved returned native-hit groups are counted as separate model components; this modeling choice is not measured sequence identity or evidence of independent experiments.
